subsystems.name: Cell source and bio-ink
subsystems.role: supplies the living cells and the gel that carries them.

subsystems.name: Print head and delivery
subsystems.role: deposits bio-ink precisely onto the wound.

subsystems.name: Imaging and mapping
subsystems.role: creates a 3D map of the wound for the printer to follow.
parts: software for depth and shape reconstruction

subsystems.name: Motion and control
subsystems.role: moves the print head over the wound surface.

subsystems.name: Crosslinking and stabilisation
subsystems.role: solidifies the printed gel so it stays in place.

subsystems.name: Sterile field integration
subsystems.role: keeps the print sterile during surgery.
parts: laminar flow or local sterile enclosure

buildSteps.title: Harvest cells
buildSteps.detail: take a small biopsy of the patient's skin or cartilage and expand the cells in a lab for weeks.

buildSteps.title: Formulate bio-ink
buildSteps.detail: mix the cells with a hydrogel and nutrients to a printable, cell-friendly consistency.

buildSteps.title: Load cartridge
buildSteps.detail: fill a sterile cartridge and keep it cold until the moment of use.

buildSteps.title: Scan the wound
buildSteps.detail: use a handheld scanner or camera to build a 3D map of the defect's shape and depth.

buildSteps.title: Print directly
buildSteps.detail: the surgeon moves the device over the wound, depositing layers of bio-ink that match the map.

buildSteps.title: Crosslink
buildSteps.detail: apply light or a crosslinker so the gel sets and the cells are held in place.

buildSteps.title: Dress and mature
buildSteps.detail: cover the printed area; over days the cells attach, multiply and remodel.

buildSteps.title: Follow up
buildSteps.detail: monitor integration, healing and function over weeks and months.

prerequisites.why: enough patient cells are needed; this is already done for skin grafts and cartilage cell therapy.
the gel must be printable, non-toxic and support cell survival.
devices have been demonstrated on animals, but not yet at scale in routine surgery.
the gel must set quickly in the operating theatre without harming the cells or the patient.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory pathway for living printed constructs
prerequisites.why: regulators have little precedent for combined device-and-cell products made at the bedside.

pathway.milestone: handheld printers in preclinical studies for burns and cartilage defects
pathway.unlocks: proof that cells survive printing and integrate with host tissue.

pathway.milestone: first controlled human trials for skin and cartilage
pathway.unlocks: safety and early efficacy data needed for approval.

pathway.milestone: robotic in-situ printing integrated into surgery for larger wounds
pathway.unlocks: faster, more consistent coverage of irregular defects.

pathway.milestone: printing more complex layered tissues with blood vessels and skin appendages
pathway.unlocks: better healing and function for severe injuries.
